entries.content_plain: Introduction The proper conclusion to the great revolutions predicted in this and the following chapters is the general resurrection, of which the beginning of this chapter (to be literally understood) gives some intimation, Dan 12:1-3 . Daniel is then commanded to shut up the words and to seal the book to the time of the end, Dan 12:4 ; and is informed of the three grand symbolical periods of a time, times, and a half, twelve hundred and ninety days and thirteen hundred and thirty-five days, Dan 12:4-12 ; at the end of the last of which Daniel shall rest and stand in his lot, Dan 12:13 . It is generally thought by commentators that the termination of the last period is the epoch of the First resurrection. See Rev 20:4 , Rev 20:5 . Verse 1 And at that time Michael shall stand up - Michael the archangel, as has already been observed, was ever reputed the guardian of the Jewish people. Every one that shall be found written in the book - All that truly fear, love, and obey the Lord, On the phrase, "written in the book, the book of life," etc., see the passages in the margin, and the notes on those passages.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen33450" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33451" type="x-p"/> And they that be wise - Those who are thoroughly instructed in Christ's word and doctrine, shall shine - shall be eminently distinguished in the Christian Church by the holiness of their lives, and the purity of their creed. <div eID="gen33451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33452" type="x-p"/> And they that turn many to righteousness - They who, by preaching Christ crucified among their brethren, shall be the means of converting them to the Christian faith; shall be as the stars - bright luminaries in the Gospel kingdom of Jesus Christ. This also may be applied to the case of holy and useful men, particularly the faithful ministers of the Gospel, in the day of judgment. See <reference osisRef="Jam.5.20">Jam 5:20</reference> (note), <reference osisRef="1Cor.15.41-1Cor.15.42">1Cor 15:41-42</reference> (note).

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen33452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33453" type="x-p"/> Shut up the words, and seal the book - When a prophet received a prediction concerning what was at a considerable distance of time, he shut his book, did not communicate his revelation for some time after. This Daniel was commanded to do, <reference osisRef="Dan.8.26">Dan 8:26</reference>. See also <reference osisRef="Isa.29.10">Isa 29:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.29.11">Isa 29:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.10">Rev 22:10</reference>. Among the ancients, those were said to seal, who in the course of their reading stamped the places of which they were yet doubtful, in order to keep them in memory, that they might refer to then; again, as not yet fully understood. This custom Salmasius, in his book De modo Usurarum, p. 446, proves from Hesychius. <div eID="gen33453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33454" type="x-p"/> Many shall run to and fro - Many shall endeavour to search out the sense; and knowledge shall be increased by these means; though the meaning shall not be fully known till the events take place: Then the seal shall be broken, and the sense become plain. This seems to be the meaning of this verse, though another has been put on it, viz., "Many shall run to and fro preaching the Gospel of Christ, and therefore religious knowledge and true wisdom shall be increased." This is true in itself; but it is not the meaning of the prophet's words.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen33458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33459" type="x-p"/> The words are closed up - The prophecy shall not be understood, but in its accomplishment; and then the depth of the wisdom and providence of God will be clearly seen in these matters. See on Daniel 4 (note). We must wait "till the time of the end;" and this, it appears from the following calculations, will not arrive before the Twentieth Century. We here see the reason why these prophecies are at present so imperfectly understood. God has sealed them.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen33459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33460" type="x-p"/> Many shall be purified - During the interim, the great work of God's providence and grace shall be carried on in the salvation of men; who, in the midst of trials, temptations, and difficulties, shall be purified and made white - be fully saved from their sins. <div eID="gen33460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33461" type="x-p"/> None of the wicked shall understand - Because they are wicked, and will continue in their sins, the eyes of their understanding shall be closed, and their hearts hardened; so that they shall not see the light of the glorious Gospel. <div eID="gen33461" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33462" type="x-p"/> But the wise - Those who open their hearts to God, that he may pour in his light, shall understand the things that make for their peace.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen33462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33463" type="x-p"/> From the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away - See the notes on <reference osisRef="Dan.11.25-Dan.11.27">Dan 11:25-27</reference> (note). <div eID="gen33463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33464" type="x-p"/> The abomination that maketh desolate set up - I believe, with Bp. Newton, that this is a proverbial phrase; and may be applied to any thing substituted in the place of, or set up in opposition to, the ordinances of God, his worship, his truth, etc. Adrian's temple, built in the place of God's temple at Jerusalem, the church of St. Sophia turned into a Mohammedan mosque, etc., etc., may be termed abominations that make desolate. Perhaps Mohammedanism may be the abomination; which sprang up a.d. 612. If we reckon one thousand two hundred and ninety years, <reference osisRef="Dan.11.11">Dan 11:11</reference>, from that time, it will bring us down to a.d. 1902, when we might presume from this calculation, that the religion of the False Prophet will cease to prevail in the world; which from the present year, 1825, is distant only seventy-seven years.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen33464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33465" type="x-p"/> Blessed is he that waiteth - He who implicitly depends on God, expecting, as his truth cannot fail, that these predictions shall be accomplished in due time. <div eID="gen33465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33466" type="x-p"/> And cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days - This is seventy-five days more than what is included in the three years and a half, or the time, times, and a half in the seventh verse; and as we have met with so many instances of prophets days and years, this undoubtedly is another instance; and as a day stands for a year, this must mean a period of one thousand three hundred and thirty-five years, which period is to bring all these wonders to an end, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.6">Dan 12:6</reference>. But we are left totally in the dark relative to the time from which these one thousand three hundred and thirty-five years are to be reckoned. If, however, we reckon them from the above epoch, a.d. 612, when Mohammedanism arose, they lead us to a.d. 1947, when the fullness of the Gentiles shall be brought in; and thus a final closure of vision and prophecy be made, as then all the great events relative to the salvation of men shall have taken place. Wars and contentions will probably then cease over the whole world; Jews and Gentiles become one fold, under one Shepherd and Bishop of souls; and the triune God be properly worshipped and glorified, from generation to generation, over the face of the whole earth. But all these conjectures may be founded in darkness. We have not chronological data; and "the times and seasons God has reserved in his own power."

navigation_sections.content_plain: Introduction The proper conclusion to the great revolutions predicted in this and the following chapters is the general resurrection, of which the beginning of this chapter (to be literally understood) gives some intimation, Dan 12:1-3 . Daniel is then commanded to shut up the words and to seal the book to the time of the end, Dan 12:4 ; and is informed of the three grand symbolical periods of a time, times, and a half, twelve hundred and ninety days and thirteen hundred and thirty-five days, Dan 12:4-12 ; at the end of the last of which Daniel shall rest and stand in his lot, Dan 12:13 . It is generally thought by commentators that the termination of the last period is the epoch of the First resurrection. See Rev 20:4 , Rev 20:5 .
navigation_sections.content_osis: <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen33444" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen33445" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen33445" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen33444" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen33446" type="x-p"/> The proper conclusion to the great revolutions predicted in this and the following chapters is the general resurrection, of which the beginning of this chapter (to be literally understood) gives some intimation, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.1-Dan.12.3">Dan 12:1-3</reference>. Daniel is then commanded to shut up the words and to seal the book to the time of the end, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.4">Dan 12:4</reference>; and is informed of the three grand symbolical periods of a time, times, and a half, twelve hundred and ninety days and thirteen hundred and thirty-five days, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.4-Dan.12.12">Dan 12:4-12</reference>; at the end of the last of which Daniel shall rest and stand in his lot, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.13">Dan 12:13</reference>. It is generally thought by commentators that the termination of the last period is the epoch of the First resurrection. See <reference osisRef="Rev.20.4">Rev 20:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.20.5">Rev 20:5</reference>. <div eID="gen33446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33447" type="x-p"/>
